$schema_note: The ONLY file in this repository allowed to know facts about the physical machine it is checked out on. Everything else derives its paths from path.resolve(__dirname, '..') and must never hardcode an absolute repository path.
purpose: Before 2026-09-04 five live code paths hardcoded 'D:\\AI\\Active FounderOS-Aidit' as the repository root. Moving the checkout (ASUS -> Lenovo, and the folder rename to 'Aidit OS') made every one of them wrong, and hatta/harness.mjs in particular refused every file operation because its security sandbox boundary pointed at a directory that no longer existed. The repository root is now always derived from the module's own location. The values below are the residue: things that genuinely live OUTSIDE the checkout and therefore cannot be derived.
rules: NEVER put a path that is inside the repository in this file. Derive it.
A consumer MUST fail loudly with the key name when a value it needs is missing, never silently fall back to a guess.
This file is machine-specific. It is committed so the shape is reviewable and the next machine move is a single-file edit, not a hunt.

node.why_pinned: Node v26 on Windows crashes at process teardown (libuv UV_HANDLE_CLOSING) AFTER tests pass, so ops-watcher/run-all-tests.mjs scores a passing suite as a failure. Measured on this machine: v26 -> 59/62, v22.14.0 -> 62/62. The system default node on PATH here is v26.5.0, so the absolute path matters.

paperclip.why_dist_entry: PM2 spawns `node <script>`. `paperclipai` on Windows is a .cmd shim, not a file node can resolve, and interpreter:'none' fails EINVAL. Pointing at the package's real dist entry is the empirically-working path. This is an internal package detail: re-confirm it after any `npm i -g paperclipai` upgrade.

cockpit.why: Tailscale Funnel hostname of THIS machine. Was 'asus-gray.tailc7b60e.ts.net' while the ASUS was the host; a stale value here makes --public screenshots and audits silently probe a machine this one cannot reach.
